author: reek
body: Database schema and operations for the issue tracker. Uses the workflow engine pattern: DbServer carries the catalog, state flows through via __record-set. Tables: issues, projects, cycles, labels. Full relational queries via Executor.

author: reek
body: These were two local wrappers, row-get-value and row-set-value, over the Data quire. The get was a pure rename of row-get-by-name and the set was the by-name setter the Row chapter did not have. Row has both now, so the wrappers are gone rather than shadowing under a second name: IssueStore called row-set-value without defining it, which is a name that resolves nowhere and a chapter that does not compile, and two chapters keeping private copies of the same helper is what makes that possible.

author: reek
body: This queried for the row, set the field, and then INSERTED the result, leaving the original in place: an update added a second row with the same id rather than replacing the first. It compiled and it ran, which is why it survived. A QueryResult carries no RowId, so there was nothing to update in place with; catalog-scan carries one and catalog-update-row takes it.
